notes: Sizing check: ENA deposits 1820 Klebsiella samples under PRJEB36683 (1554 'Klebsiella pneumoniae 11227-1', 235 K. pneumoniae, plus minor Klebsiella spp.), but the matching paper describes only 328 sequenced K. pneumoniae isolates from 239 patients (Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, 2014-2022). study_setting.evidence_quote: We will recruit 400 households in urban, peri-urban and rural settings in Malawi and Uganda.

amr_study.evidence_quote: Each household will undergo human and animal stool, and environmental sampling for ESBL E. coli and ESBL Klebsiella pneumoniae, which will be sequenced at the Wellcome Sanger Instittute.

amr_target.evidence_quote: extended spectrum betalactamase (ESBL) producing infections are locally untreatable, due to unavailability of carbapenems or other reserve antibiotics

coverage_basis: The supplied full-text paper describes Salmonella enterica isolates (341 sequenced, 270 analysed) from environmental water in Blantyre, deposited under the shared DRUM accession PRJEB37378. It describes zero Klebsiella records, so it provides no coverage of the taxon of interest (1603 Klebsiella: 1602 K. pneumoniae + 1 K. aerogenes). Grading of the Klebsiella records relies on the EBI DRUM study description.

notes: PRJEB37378 is the shared DRUM (Drivers of antimicrobial resistance in Uganda and Malawi) umbrella accession at the Wellcome Sanger Institute; the supplied full-text paper is a Salmonella enterica environmental-water study that deposited its genomes under this same project and does NOT describe any Klebsiella (taxon-of-interest) records. Grading of the 1603 Klebsiella samples therefore rests entirely on the EBI study title/description, which is a study-wide description of the whole DRUM design. DRUM is a One-Health community household study (urban/peri-urban/rural, human + animal stool + environment) in BOTH Malawi and Uganda, deliberately sampling FOR ESBL E. coli and ESBL Klebsiella pneumoniae -> community setting; amr selection on an ESBL (3GC) gate. amr_method (phenotypic AST vs PCR gene presence) is not stated in the supplied evidence; ESBL 'producing' leans phenotypic but is not nailed down, so left not_gradeable. cohort_age left not_gradeable: no explicit age data and the project mixes human household members (all ages), animals, and environmental samples. No whole-project backfill possible: two countries, multiple sources/hosts, and no Klebsiella collection dates (collection period likely >2 years).

coverage_basis: The supplied paper is a neonatal-sepsis K/O serotype meta-analysis that cites PRJEB42462 only as the source of its MLW (Malawi) study (Data availability: 'MLW, PRJEB42462'). This is ~28% of the 1302 K. pneumoniae deposited in this ENA accession, which the EBI title/description describe as a broader three-country (UK, Malawi, Argentina) >10-year longitudinal MDR-lineage study. notes: PRJEB42462 (EBI title 'Klebsiella_pneumoniae_longitudinal_study') is an umbrella accession: EBI describes three longitudinal collections (UK, Malawi, Argentina) over >10 years to identify successful MDR lineages, holding 1302 K. pneumoniae. The supplied medRxiv paper is a neonatal-sepsis K/O serotype meta-analysis that cites this accession ONLY as the source of its MLW (Malawi) study, contributing 362 neonatal blood/CSF isolates (~28% of 1302). This is the Pattern-C shared/umbrella case: study-level values verifiable from the paper apply only to the MLW neonatal subset and cannot be extended project-wide, hence partial grades. The MLW portion is hospital bloodstream/CSF surveillance of neonates, sampled as all positive cultures regardless of AMR (surveillance, not AMR-selected; rubric warns not to infer AMR from 'MDR lineage' framing). EBI shows multiple countries and a >10-year span, so country and collection_date cannot be backfilled.

notes: Sizing reconciliation: ENA total = 1806 samples, closely matching the ~1,798 ESBL-E isolates described in the EBI study description, so the deposited set equals the described collection (no major pre-sequencing selection beyond the ESBL gate). This single accession (PRJDB14656) holds 234 Klebsiella samples by itself — more than the entire 168-strain paper cohort — and the paper's blood isolates number only 85. notes: Deposited set is a deliberate three-source contrast design: hospital clinical blood-culture isolates (selected by AST profile, mostly carbapenem/ESBL-resistant) + hospital sewage (also mostly MDR) versus livestock isolates (mostly susceptible). Selection for sequencing was explicitly AST-profile-based, but susceptible livestock isolates were deliberately included to contrast against resistant human/sewage isolates -> amr_study=mixed (the 'resistant-human + susceptible-livestock' example). study_setting=mixed because hospital (clinical + hospital sewage wastewater) and community (non-human livestock) sources are both deliberately sampled. amr_target left not_gradeable as no single targeted resistance class governs selection (both ESBL/3GC and carbapenem feature heavily). cohort_age not gradeable: no human ages given and much of the project is non-human/environmental. Collection spans 2020-2022 (>2 years) so collection_date not backfilled. Article screened ~2398 clinical + 150 livestock + 21 sewage Klebsiella but deposited only ~140 (paper says 146 sequenced) -> heavy pre-sequencing selection (pattern A), consistent with the deposited subset being graded on its own composition.

amr_study.evidence_quote: One isolate per patient of any Enterobacterales species confirmed as a carbapenemase-producer from any specimen type was included.

amr_target.evidence_quote: We sequenced a total of 840 CPE that were submitted to the National CPE Reference Laboratory, Galway University Hospital, Ireland.

paper_coverage.basis: This accession is the E. coli arm of a 9-accession study (EBI title 'Carbapenemase Producing E.coli Ireland'); ENA reports 65 total samples and 0 Klebsiella samples here. The paper describes 746 CPE isolates across PRJEB19435 plus 8 other bioprojects, including 243 K. pneumoniae and 87 K. oxytoca (330 Klebsiella) — but those Klebsiella are deposited in the other accessions, not in PRJEB19435. So this accession contributes 0 taxon-of-interest (Klebsiella) records.

raw.notes: Sizing reconciliation: ENA shows E=65 total samples and E_taxon=0 for Klebsiella; by_scientific_name is empty. EBI title/description = 'Carbapenemase Producing E.coli Ireland', i.e. this is the E. coli accession of a multi-accession study. Paper's sequenced cohort (746 isolates) is far larger than E=65 -> Pattern B: the study spans multiple accessions (PRJEB19435, PRJEB22264, PRJEB19229, PRJEB24082-24087) and this is only one of them. The 330 Klebsiella (243 K. pneumoniae + 87 K. oxytoca) described in the paper are deposited in the OTHER accessions, not here, so this accession holds no taxon-of-interest records. Study-level design (national CPE reference-lab collection of confirmed carbapenemase-producers, from 33 Irish hospitals, 2012-2017) is uniform across the whole study and is fully described by the paper, so study-level attributes are graded gradeable for the project. amr_study = amr: every isolate had to be a confirmed carbapenemase-producer to be sequenced (a resistance gate), making this AMR-selected rather than all-clinical surveillance. amr_method left not_gradeable: the text does not state whether carbapenemase confirmation that gated selection was phenotypic (AST) or molecular/PCR — ARIBA gene detection in the paper was downstream characterization, not the selection criterion. collection_date period (Apr 2012-Jun 2017) exceeds 2 years, so not backfilled.

coverage_basis: Klebsiella in this project = ESBL-Kp. Paper reports the full deposited cohort of 2275 isolates from 1970 patients, of which ESBL-Kp = 189 isolates (9.4%). The paper describes the entire BioProject PRJNA565795, so it covers ~100% of the project's Klebsiella records.

country.evidence_quote: in eight hospitals from four hospital networks, including approximately 2800 acute and subacute inpatient beds, in Melbourne, Australia

isolation_source.evidence_quote: After screening swabs (37·1%), urine (20·4%), and swabs from non-sterile sites (20·4%) were the most common sample types, with only 6·9% of isolates being from blood cultures

host.evidence_quote: collected routinely from hospital inpatients (>24 h) at any time during their admission

collection_date.evidence_quote: a pilot phase (24th April–18th June 2017), and an implementation phase (30th October 2017–30th November 2018), totalling 15 months

notes: ENA sizing returns 0 samples/0 runs because PRJNA565795 is an NCBI SRA BioProject not mirrored to ENA; the deposited set per the paper's data-sharing statement is the 2275 study isolates (1970 patients) across four MDROs. Klebsiella subset = ESBL-Kp = 189 isolates. Selection gate is AMR-based: only ESBL-phenotype K. pneumoniae were included (no susceptible Klebsiella controls), so amr (not surveillance/mixed); ESBL = 3GC; established by phenotypic AST. study_setting=hospital (all hospital inpatients, clinical + screening). cohort_age left not_gradeable: only an aggregate cross-species statistic is given (median 65, IQR 47-77) which leans adult, but network B includes a specialist pediatric hospital with neonatal ICU and all inpatients were eligible, so a single age band cannot be confirmed for the whole project and no Klebsiella-specific ages are provided (plausibly mixed). collection_date backfilled to the ~19-month window midpoint (≤2 years).

notes: Multi-accession study (pattern B): the paper deposits 168 clinical K. pneumoniae genomes across four BioProjects (PRJDB12075, PRJDB12116, PRJDB14656, PRJDB17849); PRJDB17849 holds only a subset and the exact count for this accession is not separable in the paper. ENA Stage-1 sizing returned all zeros for this accession (no ENA-mirrored records), consistent with a DDBJ-registered project not yet present in ENA. All isolates are described uniformly as Japanese clinical K. pneumoniae collected 2015-2018, so qualitative study-level attributes (hospital setting, surveillance sampling rule, country=Japan, human host) apply to the whole accession. No AMR-based selection: all non-redundant clinical isolates were sequenced for a pathogenicity/virulence study, so amr_study=surveillance and amr_target/amr_method are not applicable. Collection period spans >2 years (Jan 2015-Apr 2018), so collection_date is not backfilled. Age data unavailable (de-identified strains).
